scenes.title: Keep the original private
scenes.narration: A hiring team needs course completion, not your whole certificate. In Facet, I upload training notes into a password-protected local vault.

scenes.title: A record is not a qualification
scenes.narration: I create a private document NFT. The original stays on my device. This self-recorded fingerprint is explicitly unverified; uploading does not authenticate it.

scenes.title: Claims signed by an issuer
scenes.narration: Now I issue a fictional training credential from Facet Test Academy. Its claims have a real BBS signature and a holder-bound NEAR record.

scenes.title: Ask only for what matters
scenes.narration: The example hiring team requests just the course and completion status. The request binds its purpose, selected fields and a short-lived, single-use nonce.

scenes.title: The holder controls disclosure
scenes.narration: Before approving, I can see exactly what is shared. Course and completion are revealed. The name, score, date and student reference stay hidden.

scenes.title: Export a selective proof
scenes.narration: I approve and export the proof. The real exported package excludes the hidden name and score, and includes the required public credential bindings.

scenes.title: Verify on a separate device
scenes.narration: In a separate browser, the verifier imports my proof without opening a vault or receiving the original document. Then they run the verification checks.

scenes.title: A useful answer, with evidence
scenes.narration: The proof checks out. The verifier sees Data Privacy Foundations and Completed. A genuine NEAR transaction records the single-use verification receipt.

scenes.title: NEAR provides shared current status
scenes.narration: The checks cover signatures, holder approval and live status. NEAR anchors issuer keys, expiry, revocation and nonce use. BBS math runs outside the contract.

scenes.title: Check the rejection paths
scenes.narration: The proof lab runs real positive and negative checks, including altered claims and holder substitution. All eight behave as expected. Used requests cannot be replayed.

scenes.title: Stop future verification
scenes.narration: I generate a fresh unused proof, then revoke the credential. Revocation changes its current NEAR status. It cannot erase information already shared.

scenes.title: A fresh proof is now rejected
scenes.narration: That unused proof now fails specifically because of revocation. Facet demonstrates useful credential NFTs with controlled disclosure. Try the live testnet app and inspect the public code.
